tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigates the Magento Admin Shipments grid (table#sales_shipment_grid), fills filter inputs (Shipment #, Order #, Ship to Name, Total Qty From/To), clicks Search, selects the matching row checkbox, chooses a mass-action (PDF Packingslips or Print Shipping Labels) and submits it, selects an export format (CSV/Excel/XML) and triggers Export, then opens a specific shipment View (by id). The tool will re-run these deterministic actions using the stable selectors captured during recording.

Task Definition:
- Build a reusable, deterministic automation tool that: 1) loads the Shipments grid, 2) applies provided filters, 3) runs Search, 4) selects the matched shipment row, 5) runs a mass-action, 6) exports the (filtered) results in a chosen format, and 7) opens a specific shipment View page.

Action Plan (step-by-step):
1) Navigate to the Shipments grid URL: {base_url}/index.php/admin/sales_shipment/
2) Fill Shipment # filter with {shipment_increment} (stable element recorded)
3) Fill Order # filter with {order_increment}
4) Fill Ship to Name filter with {ship_to_name}
5) Fill Total Qty From with {total_qty_from}
6) Fill Total Qty To with {total_qty_to}
7) Click the Search button to apply filters
8) Wait short period for server response
9) Click the checkbox for the matched row (first/recorded row match)
10) Select the mass-action option {massaction} from the Actions select
11) Click the mass-action Submit button
12) Wait short period for the mass-action to complete
13) Select export format {export_format} from the Export select
14) Click the Export button to download/export the filtered results
15) Navigate to the chosen shipment View page using {view_shipment_db_id}

Variable Identification (inputs):
- base_url: anchor for all navigation
- shipment_increment: populates Shipment # filter
- order_increment: populates Order # filter
- ship_to_name: populates Ship to Name filter
- total_qty_from / total_qty_to: numeric range filter values
- massaction: exact visible option text for the mass-action dropdown
- export_format: visible export option text (CSV/Excel/XML)
- view_shipment_db_id: numeric DB id used to open the shipment View URL

Step Optimization and Selector Choices:
- Navigation uses a direct URL instead of clicking UI menus for repeatability.
- Filter inputs and action buttons use the recorded elementHash values (stable selectors captured during the live session) to avoid brittle nth-child CSS when possible.
- Mass-action and Export use select_change actions by visible text for clarity and to match recorded selection.
- The final View uses direct URL navigation (deterministic) rather than relying on a per-row View link that may move with sorting/pagination.
- All steps are strictly necessary for the single task (no optional exploratory steps). The tool assumes the admin session is already authenticated in the browser context executing the tool. If the environment blocks JavaScript or requires form_key for some POST actions, the tool uses the UI controls as recorded which worked in the session; troubleshooting instructions are documented in the session notes but not included as conditional flows here.

Notes on robustness:
- Selectors were chosen from recorded element interactions to ensure uniqueness. When reusing this tool against another Magento install, replace the element hashes or update the elementHash mapping if the admin theme or grid id differs. The tool prefers direct navigation for view and grid access for reliability.
name: magento_admin_shipments_tool
description: Automates locating shipments in Magento Admin (Shipments grid) using provided filters, performs export, executes a mass-action (e.g., PDF Packingslips), and opens a specific shipment View. Uses the stable selectors recorded during a live session on a Magento 1.9.x admin installation. Assumes the caller is already authenticated in the admin session.

steps.description: Open the Shipments grid page in the admin panel.
Fill the 'Ship to Name' filter input (recorded element).
Fill the 'Total Qty' filter 'From' input (recorded element).
Fill the 'Total Qty' filter 'To' input (recorded element).
Click the 'Search' button to apply the filters.
Wait for the server to apply filters and render results.
Click the checkbox for the matched row (recorded row checkbox element).
Choose the mass-action from the Actions dropdown (e.g., 'PDF Packingslips').
Click the mass-action Submit button to run the selected action.
Wait for the mass-action to complete on the server.
Select the desired export format from the Export control above the grid.
Click the Export button to download/export the grid in the chosen format.
Open the shipment View page for the provided internal shipment DB id.

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base URL of the Magento admin site, e.g. 'http://dockerized-magento.local'. Do NOT include a trailing slash.

input_schema.name: shipment_increment
input_schema.description: Shipment increment/display number to filter by (example: '100000032'). This fills the 'Shipment #' filter input.

input_schema.name: order_increment
input_schema.description: Order increment/display number to filter by (example: '100000199'). This fills the 'Order #' filter input.

input_schema.name: ship_to_name
input_schema.description: Recipient name to filter the 'Ship to Name' column (example: 'Jane Doe').

input_schema.name: total_qty_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for 'Total Qty' filter (use a numeric string, e.g. '1').

input_schema.name: total_qty_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for 'Total Qty' filter (use a numeric string, e.g. '1').

input_schema.name: massaction
input_schema.description: Visible text of the mass-action to execute from the Actions dropdown (exact visible option text).

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Export format to choose from the Export control above the grid.

input_schema.name: view_shipment_db_id
input_schema.description: Numeric internal shipment DB id to open the shipment View page (used to navigate directly). Example: for View URL '/.../view/shipment_id/35/' supply '35'.
